claims.claim: Israeli capital gains tax on securities: 25% for individuals (Section 91(b)(1)), 30% for substantial shareholders >10% (Section 91(b)(2)), 23% corporate (Section 126(a)); plus a surtax (mas yesef, Section 121B) of up to 5% (3% base + 2% from 2025) on capital income above ~721,560 NIS/yr (2025-2027).

claims.claim: Israeli dividend tax on TASE securities: 25% for an individual non-substantial shareholder, 30% for a substantial shareholder (>10%), withheld at source (nikui b'makor). Surtax (mas yesef) also applies to dividend income above the annual threshold. Foreign-brokerage holders self-report on Form 1322 / טופס 1322 (capital gains) and Form 1301 / טופס 1301 (annual return). Israel has no annual tax-free capital-gains allowance.

claims.claim: For securities gains on which full Israeli tax was NOT withheld at source (a foreign brokerage, or an Israeli company's shares traded on a foreign exchange), an Israeli resident must file a semi-annual report and pay a capital-gains advance (mikdama) by 31 January and 31 July for gains realized in the preceding six months, under Section 91(d) of the Income Tax Ordinance. Late payment accrues interest and CPI linkage.
